pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: Extreme delta brush pattern on EEG combined with pelvic ultrasound revealing a mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) of the ovary PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient suffers from an autoimmune encephalitis triggered by ectopic neural tissue contained within an ovarian teratoma. The host immune system recognizes this neural tissue as foreign and mounts an antibody response targeting the GluN1 subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. These IgG antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier, causing cross-linking and selective internalization of cell-surface NMDA receptors in the central nervous system. This causes a dramatic reduction in NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic function, disrupting frontostriatal network inhibition. The clinical progression classically advances from psychiatric disturbances to memory loss, seizures, movement disorders (characteristic orofacial dyskinesias), severe dysautonomia, and central hypoventilation. Definitive treatment requires surgical resection of the underlying teratoma combined with aggressive immunosuppression (high-dose corticosteroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis, and rituximab).
